---
title: "Equations and numerical methods"
---

## GLM magnetohydrodynamics {#sec-glm}

The MHD state stores nine conserved fields in structure-of-arrays order
`(rho, rho*vx, rho*vy, rho*vz, E, Bx, By, Bz, psi)`. Code magnetic units absorb
`4*pi`, so magnetic pressure is `B^2/2`, not `B^2/(8*pi)`.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/state.jl" "allocate_state" >}}

The local ideal-MHD flux operator has continuity, momentum, and induction terms

$$
\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v)=0,
\qquad
\partial_t(\rho\mathbf v)+\nabla\cdot\left[
\rho\mathbf v\mathbf v+(p+B^2/2)\mathbf I-\mathbf B\mathbf B\right]
=\mathbf S_m,
$$ {#eq-mhd-momentum}

$$
\partial_t\mathbf B+\nabla\cdot(\mathbf v\mathbf B-\mathbf B\mathbf v)
+\nabla\psi=0,
\qquad
p=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{\rho v^2}{2}-\frac{B^2}{2}\right).
$$ {#eq-induction}

Here the induction tensor is understood componentwise as the flux
`v_j B_i - B_j v_i` in direction `j`. The GLM scalar propagates magnetic
divergence at the cleaning speed and is damped by the mixed hyperbolic/parabolic
cleaning update. The energy flux is
`(E+p+B^2/2)*v - (v dot B)*B`; external gravity, drag, expansion-aware chemistry,
and radiation response are coupled by their respective source updates, not
inserted as an unqualified isolated-box conservation law.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/glm_physics.jl" "glm" >}}

The production scheme uses finite-volume Godunov updates with PPM reconstruction
and HLLD [@miyoshi2005] with GLM cleaning [@dedner2002] unless configured
otherwise; PLM is used by the tiny installation
examples. LLF fallback and positivity handling can change the local numerical
diffusion and must be monitored. A portable reference integrator and fused cube
integrator coexist. Shared source is not a substitute for backend parity tests.

## Constrained transport (optional) {#sec-ct}

`mhd_solver = "ct"` replaces the GLM divergence cleaning by face-staggered
constrained transport [@gardiner2005]; GLM stays the default. The Godunov
sweeps are shared with GLM: PLM/PPM reconstruction, the Hancock predictor, and
HLLD/HLL/LLF fluxes on cell-centred conserved variables, with the normal
magnetic component at each face overwritten by the staggered face value and
`psi` identically zero. The induction update differs:

1. The Godunov magnetic fluxes on the lower faces give face EMFs, and a
   cell-centred reference EMF `E = -v x B` is built from the source-updated
   predicted velocity and the step-start `B`.
2. Edge EMFs are the Gardiner and Stone CT-contact average of the four adjacent
   face EMFs, with upwind gradient corrections selected by the sign of the
   mass flux and anchored on the cell-centred reference EMF.
3. The face fields `bxf, byf, bzf` advance by the discrete curl of the edge
   EMFs, so the face divergence is preserved to round-off.
4. The cell-centred `B` used by every other module (energy, forces, chemistry,
   radiation, diagnostics) is the average of the two faces.

The scheme is a port of `ct_mhd.jl` from the Solaceonx/GLMMHDTurb sweep-fixes
(commits `9d20e52` and `7256715`).
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/ct.jl" "_ct_gs05" >}}

Initial conditions are generated as a cell field. Once all initial-condition and
import stages are complete, the driver builds divergence-free faces from it once
with the minimal change of the cell field (projection onto the face-solenoidal
subspace with the `tan(k dx/2)` symbol), keeps the thermal pressure fixed, and
logs `CT_INITIAL_FACES cell_b_rel_l2_change`, `magnetic_energy_ratio`, and
`divb_face_dx_over_brms`. Because the PMF generators make the field solenoidal
under another discrete symbol (centred `sin 2θ`, or continuum `θ`), this
changes the field by O((k dx)^2) near the cutoff. The measured rms
(`brms_measured`) reports the post-projection cell field; the reference-band
normalization values remain those of the generated field.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/ct.jl" "ct_faces_from_cells!" >}}

**Limits.** CT is periodic-only and implemented on the `ref` integrator only; the
`cube` integrators, terminal and hybrid drag, and the GLM projection are
rejected. Metal allows 31 buffer arguments per kernel and counts each scalar
argument as one, so the CT kernel (`step_ref_ct_kernel!`, generated from the same
body as the GLM `step_ref_kernel!`) takes the 18 CT arrays as one packed buffer
and the grid/BC integers as one tuple; it runs on Metal. (GLM's `ref` kernel
still exceeds the limit on Metal, as before CT; GLM runs there use `cube`.)
CUDA is `NOT_RUN`. CT allocates 18 extra `N^3` arrays (three face fields and 15
flux/EMF workspace arrays, in one buffer) on top of GLM's 18. From a state at
rest the face mass fluxes are rounding noise and the upwind choice of the edge
EMF follows their sign, so CT trajectories on different devices separate at
first faster than with a definite flow (Metal vs CPU Float32, 32^3 PMF field,
20 steps: 1.2e-4 relative from rest, 1.3e-6 with a uniform flow). The explicit step is not limited by the
GLM cleaning speed. `divb_face_dx_over_brms` in `history.tsv` and
`performance.tsv` is the exact face divergence (empty/`NaN` for GLM); the
centred `divBdx_over_brms` is a different diagnostic and is not zero for CT.

## Magnetic-force decomposition {#sec-force-split}

The centered Maxwell-stress diagnostic uses

$$
\mathbf F_P=-\nabla(B^2/2),\qquad
\mathbf F_T=\nabla\cdot(\mathbf B\mathbf B),\qquad
\mathbf F_L=\mathbf F_P+\mathbf F_T.
$$ {#eq-maxwell}

The divergence form equals `(B dot grad) B` only when magnetic divergence is
negligible. The force used by the radiation coupling and diagnostic split uses
the same centered stencil.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/terminal_ct.jl" "terminal_magnetic_force_split!" >}}

## Expansion, units, and clocks {#sec-clocks}

The run evolves `a=1/(1+z)` and a dimensionless supercomoving clock `tau` with

$$
\frac{da}{d\tau}=
\sqrt{a^3\left(\Omega_m+\Omega_\Lambda a^3+\Omega_k a+\Omega_r/a\right)},
\qquad \Omega_k=1-\Omega_m-\Omega_\Lambda-\Omega_r.
$$ {#eq-clock}

Radiation density is included in early starts. The driver converts this clock
to physical source times and MHD code time; it does **not** equate an MHD step
to a physical second. `legacy` and `jedamzik` clock scalings are distinct
model choices, with the facade using the latter for cosmological runs.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "dadtau" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _hydro_time_per_tau" >}}

For a comoving field amplitude in nG specified at `z_ref`, the initializer uses

$$
B_{\rm phys}=10^{-9}B_{0,\rm nG}(1+z_{\rm ref})^2\ {\rm G},\qquad
B_{\rm code}=\frac{B_{\rm phys}}{v_{\rm unit}\sqrt{4\pi\rho_b(z_{\rm ref})}}.
$$ {#eq-field-units}

`3 pG = 0.003 nG`. The physical density follows the selected baryon cosmology.
`MHD_CHEM_VUNIT` is in cm/s; it is not a box velocity in km/s. The pressure
initializer with `pressure="auto"` uses the same CMB convention as the
chemistry, `T_CMB=2.725(1+z) K`, including particle-number contributions from
helium and electrons.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _pmf_code_brms_from_comoving_ng" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _cosmological_ionized_p0" >}}

The TOML box is ckpc/h. The facade divides it by `h` for the driver's comoving
ckpc length. The diagnostic spectrum has a separate numeric box parameter;
see [wavenumber units](notation.qmd#sec-wavenumbers) before plotting it.

## Photon-baryon response {#sec-photon-model}

The evolved-moment closure retains photon density and three photon velocity
components. In its linear Fourier response subproblem, consistent code-time
derivatives obey

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_b'&=-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf v_b,\\
\mathbf v_b'&=-i\mathbf k c_s^2\delta_b+
\Gamma(\mathbf v_\gamma-\mathbf v_b)+\mathbf F_{\rm MHD},\\
\delta_\gamma'&=-\tfrac43 i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf v_\gamma,\\
\mathbf v_\gamma'&=-\tfrac14 i c^2\mathbf k\delta_\gamma+
R\Gamma(\mathbf v_b-\mathbf v_\gamma)-S_\gamma(k)\mathbf v_\gamma,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-photon-moments}

where `R=3*rho_b*c^2/(4*rho_gamma_energy)` and `Gamma` is the converted
Compton-drag rate. Equal and opposite scattering momentum transfers recover
the tight-coupling sound speed `c^2/[3(1+R)]`. An algebraic nonlocal stress
closure replaces independent quadrupole fields, approaching diffusion damping
at small `k*lambda_gamma` and phase mixing toward free streaming.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/radiation_coupling.jl" "_photon_stress_rates" >}}

`moments` uses a second-order L-stable SDIRK response; `moments_exponential`
is the exponential variant chosen by the facade. They should not be described
as identical integrators. Legacy `angular` and `bridge` models remain comparison
options, not higher-order photon hierarchies.

The full MHD update remains active. Spectral predictors and correctors adjust
both density and velocity relative to local drag, avoiding double-counting its
effect. Default photon ICs are adiabatic and comoving with gas; controls are
`MHD_RADIATION_PHOTON_ADIABATIC` and `MHD_RADIATION_PHOTON_COMOVING`.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/radiation_coupling.jl" "step_radiation_godunov!" >}}

The positive `MHD_RADIATION_FREE_STREAM_TOL` optimization can omit the spectral
gas correction when its bound is small, while still evolving photons. Compare
against zero tolerance before interpreting its accuracy or speed.

## Gravity and chemistry {#sec-gravity-chemistry}

The periodic Poisson solve removes the homogeneous source and combines gas and
lattice-DM perturbations with the configured baryon/DM weights. The default
midpoint density source and particle updates are time-centered. Lattice
displacements reduce cancellation when tiny density perturbations are evolved;
they are not an imported cosmological particle realization.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/gravity_coupling.jl" "gravity" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "_assemble_total_perturbation_k!" >}}

The full mixing chemistry couples hydrogen/helium abundances, thermal energy,
and recombination response. The facade uses symmetric half-steps around MHD and
an expansion-aware source clock. Centered hydrogen storage protects small
perturbations relative to a changing homogeneous ionization reference; it must
be reconstructed before interpreting an abundance array as `x_HII`.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "chem_hydrogen_storage" >}}

Gaussian smoothing approximates mixing. Optional nonlocal response tables add
a separately modeled, support-limited response. Neither path solves full
three-dimensional Lyman-alpha transfer; [validation limits](validation.qmd#sec-limitations)
are part of the model specification.

## Baryon–DM streaming and planar studies {#sec-streaming}

A particle velocity is not an MHD velocity. The periodic particle solver stores
$u_c=dx/d\tau$ with $d\tau=H_0dt/a^2$, so its physical peculiar velocity is
$v_c=(H_0 L/a)u_c$, where $L$ is the **physical comoving box length**, independent
of the spectral coordinate box. In Jedamzik scaling the gas conversion is
$v_b=v_{\rm unit}\sqrt{a_{\rm ref}/a}\,u_b$. The gas momentum decay
$u_b\propto a^{-1/2}$ and constant force-free particle $u_c$ both give physical
$v\propto a^{-1}$. Their gravitational impulses agree after these conversions.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "_particle_velocity_cms_per_code" >}}
{{< test "test/inherited/test_pmf_checkpoint_helpers.jl" "baryon-DM common physical clocks" >}}

The optional `[streaming]` components `vx_kms`, `vy_kms`, and `vz_kms` specify
physical peculiar **baryon minus DM** velocity at `cosmology.zstart`. The built-in
initial state uses the DM rest frame: gas receives this uniform boost, preserving
its internal energy, and DM begins at rest. No normalization epoch is inferred.
Photons follow the existing comoving-gas initialization unless
`MHD_RADIATION_PHOTON_COMOVING=false` is explicitly selected. That choice changes
the photon rest frame and must be included in an experiment's specification.
Streaming requires cosmology, full gravity with gas kicks, and Jedamzik scaling;
a boost is rejected with an imported correlated state to avoid adding it twice.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/streaming.jl" "boost_gas_velocity!" >}}

[Tseliakhovich & Hirata (2010)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2416) describe the
coupling of coherent relative flows to short density modes. The supplied boost
is a local controlled background, not a draw from their cosmological distribution.
The built-in PMF gas/DM initialization is uniform in density and has no primordial
adiabatic transfer realization. Its growing DM perturbations are PMF-driven.
A cosmological suppression measurement needs correlated density, velocity, thermal
and photon initial conditions and matched zero-stream controls. It also needs
phase-sensitive density growth at common epochs and separate timestep/grid
convergence. A plot of streaming RMS cannot establish that measurement.

`tools/reference/streaming.py` supplies an independent **REFERENCE_ONLY**
moving-background ODE in the DM frame, with matter-only expansion and prescribed
adiabatic sound speed. Its analytic growing-mode, transverse-stream and conjugate
phase tests check conventions; they do not certify the nonlinear coupled solver.
{{< test "test/python/test_streaming.py" >}}

`magnetic.invariant_axis=1|2|3` retains only magnetic modes with zero wavenumber
along that axis before normalization. All three magnetic and velocity components
remain active. This defines planar (2.5D) initial conditions evolved by the existing
3D periodic cube kernels. It still allocates and updates **N cubed** cells; it is
not an N-by-N-by-1 accelerated solver. The planar spectrum is a different ensemble
from isotropic 3D Batchelor statistics, so do not interpret its 3D shell estimates
as an isotropic cosmological spectrum. Uniform streaming, uniform chemistry, and
the periodic lattice respect this symmetry analytically; tests check numerical
invariance. Imported states require their own symmetry checks.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/pmf.jl" "pmf_batchelor_field" >}}
{{< test "test/streaming_checks.jl" >}}
